method.authorization: Start the official CLI in an isolated HOME with SSH_CONNECTION set; select Google OAuth; read the printed authorization URL without completing sign-in. PKCE, state and other transient login values are omitted.
method.modelDiscovery: Use a synthetic consumer token in an isolated HOME, override CLOUD_CODE_URL to a local HTTP mock, and run the official models subcommand. No real Google credential is supplied. The mock's Argon entry is a fixture, not evidence of live model access.
method.accountScopes: Refresh the two existing plugin accounts through their configured routing; query Google's tokeninfo endpoint; retain only scope names and the boolean OAuth-client match. No account/token material is included.

conclusions: The plugin's OAuth scope list is missing aicode compared with the observed official CLI login.
Refreshing an existing token does not add an OAuth grant omitted from the authorization request. Reauthorization is required to request aicode.
The official CLI request User-Agent differs from both the plugin's short User-Agent and its Electron bootstrap User-Agent.
The historical claim that every CLI 1.x identity is retired is not established: previous short/hub-shaped request tests did not test this observed official CLI identity.
The model discovery path and project body match the plugin. The observation does not establish the official client's production endpoint selection.

The controlled live discovery test identifies User-Agent as a model-discovery gate for this account: captured CLI returns Argon while legacy Electron does not. Aicode was absent in both, so it is not required for this observed access.
limitations: Missing aicode is a confirmed authorization drift but did not prevent the observed Argon discovery, quota or generation. It must not be described as the demonstrated root cause.
Explicit openid was observed with the official HTTPS callback. Its compatibility with the plugin's loopback callback has not been measured, so this change does not add it.
The generation request was not captured: the isolated fake-token run stopped at external userinfo TLS validation.
No Hub/IDE identity or credential migration is implemented. The canonical CLI headers override legacy fingerprint values at every Cloud Code call.
No causal claim about account restrictions follows from these observations.

implementation.headers: All Cloud Code model, quota, bootstrap and generation calls use the captured CLI version/changelist together. No random SDK client header. The proxy transport rejects duplicate/noncanonical User-Agent and uncontracted identifying headers.
implementation.generationEvidence: The official generation path has not been captured. Reusing the captured control-plane CLI identity is an explicit implementation choice; it has now been accepted by live Argon generation.
implementation.versionPolicy: Pinned observed CLI build; a feed alone cannot change the version independently of changelist. Stored legacy fingerprints cannot affect Cloud Code headers.

liveVerification.method: Same active account, same refreshed token, same daily endpoint and project; only User-Agent changed. No aicode permission on this token.

limitations: The current backend log was locked/empty; the 2.31.2 log belongs to an earlier launch, not a proved version of the current PID.
No PC credential was exported and no official IDE generation request headers were captured.
pcIdeComparison.pluginRoute: CLI-authenticated Cloud Code JSON REST with captured CLI identity; not the IDE Hub backend

pickerRoutingRegression.symptom: After discovery, cachedModels contains concrete -low/-medium/-high ids while the picker exposes their unified base id; getSession(base) returned undefined before dispatch.
pickerRoutingRegression.fix: Recognize unified base ids backed by at least two exact discovered variants; choose only published wire levels.
